report_markdown:
**Evidence pack: Ledgerly AP automation for a CFO at a 400-person US manufacturer**
Compare against the buyer’s current AP process; no incumbent or baseline was specified. Checked 2026-11-14 using only the six supplied test-page captures. Cost evidence supports investigation, not a buyer-specific return. Audit evidence supports conditional reliance, not guaranteed acceptance. Independent sources do not verify Ledgerly’s savings or claimed SOC reports.

### It costs too much for what we'd save
_In the buyer's words:_ "Show me net savings after subscription, implementation and internal effort—not a headline ROI from a different business."

| Claim | Source | Fit | Date | Independence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Median fully loaded cost per invoice: $9.87 for mostly manual teams; $2.36 for the top quartile of automated teams. Survey of 410 US companies, including 96 manufacturing respondents; no manufacturing-only breakout or before-and-after comparison. | [AP Benchmarks](https://apbenchmarks.example/2026/cost-per-invoice) | partial: US sample includes manufacturing, but aggregate results and no size breakdown | 2026-03 | third_party |
| Cost per invoice fell from $9.40 to $3.10 over 12 months after go-live. Tern Logistics: 600-person US freight company, 9,000 invoices monthly; measured by its finance team. | [Ledgerly — Tern Logistics](https://ledgerly.example/customers/tern-logistics) | partial: similar size and same country, different industry | 2026-04 | vendor |
| “Implementation took five months, not the six weeks we were promised.” One controller review from a 250–500-employee manufacturer; cost impact undisclosed. | [Ledgerly reviews — manufacturing controller](https://reviews.example/products/ledgerly) | strong: same industry and similar size; geography unspecified | 2026-08 | third_party |
| 212% ROI over three years and payback in under 7 months. Ledgerly-commissioned Northfield Research study; four customer interviews combined into a 1,000-employee composite. | [Northfield Research — commissioned TEI](https://ledgerly.example/resources/tei-study) | weak: larger composite, industry and geography unspecified; only supplied ROI/payback source | 2025-09 | vendor |

- Suggest using AP Benchmarks to frame opportunity, not predict savings: it compares different groups. Tern offers a Ledgerly before-and-after result, but neither establishes this buyer’s baseline or net savings.
- Treat Northfield’s commissioned ROI as a hypothesis to test, not an independent forecast or a result for this manufacturer.
- Acknowledge the manufacturing controller’s five-month implementation versus six weeks promised. Seek a scoped rollout and all implementation costs before claiming payback.

**Ask:** Tern reported cost per invoice falling from $9.40 to $3.10; what are your current fully loaded cost per invoice and monthly invoice volume, using a consistent cost definition?

### Our auditors won't accept automated approvals
_In the buyer's words:_ "Can our auditors rely on the approval controls and evidence, or will we still need a parallel manual process?"

| Claim | Source | Fit | Date | Independence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| “The approval audit trail made our audit easy.” One controller review from a 250–500-employee manufacturer; no auditor opinion or testing details supplied. | [Ledgerly reviews — manufacturing controller](https://reviews.example/products/ledgerly) | strong: same industry and similar size; one experience, not assurance | 2026-08 | third_party |
| An auditor may rely on an automated control when general IT controls have been tested and are effective, and the control is tested once in the period. System-enforced approval is the example. | [ASB staff Q&A](https://asb.example/staff-qa/automated-controls) | weak: no segment match; only supplied standards guidance on reliance | 2025-11 | third_party |
| Ledgerly says it holds SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II reports; approval records include approver, timestamp and policy rule. SOC 1 period ended June 30, 2026; SOC 2 period unspecified. Reports under NDA, not supplied. | [Ledgerly Trust center](https://ledgerly.example/trust) | weak: no segment-specific scope; only direct report and record statement | 2026-11-14, capture date; page undated | vendor |

- Cite the ASB staff Q&A against a blanket rejection, not as a guarantee: reliance requires effective tested IT controls and control testing. The buyer’s auditor confirms applicability.
- Use Ledgerly’s trust page to request the actual reports and sample approval records. The buyer’s auditor confirms scope, exceptions, coverage and required customer controls; the page is not assurance.
- Offer the manufacturing controller’s audit-trail comment as a relevant peer experience, not an audit opinion. The same reviewer reported a longer-than-promised implementation.

**Ask:** Given the ASB Q&A’s testing conditions, how many approval controls would your auditor need to assess, and how many currently have documented IT-control and in-period testing evidence?

### What cuts against you
- A manufacturing controller reported five months to implement versus six weeks promised. This challenges rollout assumptions, though no cost impact is quantified. ([Ledgerly reviews](https://reviews.example/products/ledgerly), 2026-08)
- Auditor reliance is conditional on tested, effective general IT controls and in-period automated-control testing—not automatic acceptance. ([ASB staff Q&A](https://asb.example/staff-qa/automated-controls), 2025-11)

### Gaps
- **Cost:** The supplied customer result and ROI study are vendor evidence. The independent benchmark does not verify Ledgerly-specific savings. Pricing, buyer baseline and independently verified manufacturing savings are missing. Close with a scoped quote, all-in implementation estimates, consistent buyer baseline and a comparable manufacturer's documented results.
- **Audit:** The trust page is not the underlying SOC reports. The Q&A and one review do not verify Ledgerly’s report scope, exceptions, approval-record integrity or this buyer’s auditor acceptance. Close with the reports, coverage updates, control documentation and sample records; the buyer’s auditor confirms reliance requirements.

### Do next
- Prepare an invoice-cost and approval-effort baseline worksheet for Tuesday; do not calculate savings before definitions align.
- Request a scoped quote and rollout plan, including internal effort, dependencies and acceptance criteria; test the reported delay concern.
- Obtain SOC reports, coverage updates and sample approval evidence for the buyer’s auditor.
- Request a comparable manufacturing reference and the commissioned study’s assumptions; separate customer outcomes from composite projections.
